chunks: With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

My father wrote in his will that I should shroud him in three garments: one of them a striped cloak belonging to him in which he used to pray on Friday, another cloth, and a shirt. So I said to my father, “Why do you write this?” He said, “I fear that people may prevail over you; so if they say: shroud him in four garments or five, then do not do it.”
He said: “And afterward, place a turban upon me; but the turban is not counted as part of the shroud. Rather, what is counted is that by which the body is wrapped.”

key_terms.أُكَفِّنُهُ: I shroud him for burial in the prescribed kafan
key_terms.الْجَسَدُ: the body of the deceased which is wrapped by the shroud
key_terms.الْكَفَنِ: the burial shroud prescribed for the deceased
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةِ أَثْوَابٍ: three garments that constitute the shroud
key_terms.حِبَرَةٌ: a striped Yemeni-style cloak used here as one shrouding garment
key_terms.عِمَامَةٍ: a turban placed after shrouding, but not counted within the kafan
key_terms.وَصِيَّتِهِ: his testamentary instruction concerning burial preparation

ai.seo_question: How many garments are included in the kafan, and is the turban counted as part of it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal instruction regarding the kafan, specifying that it consists of three garments and warning against adding more due to social pressure. It also clarifies that a turban may be added afterward, but it is not counted as part of the kafan because the kafan is what wraps the body itself.
